title: Block: Binary Search on the Answer
oneLiner: Find the smallest ship capacity that delivers packages in order within a number of days, by binary searching over capacities.
keyTakeaway: When "does X work?" is easy and the answers are monotonic (if X works, so does X + 1), binary search over X with a feasibility check. The block is the check plus the lower-bound loop.
explanation:
weights must be shipped in order, one day at a time; a day's load can't exceed the ship's capacity. Return the smallest capacity that ships everything within days days. [1..10] in 5 days needs 15.

The answer lies between the heaviest package (anything smaller can't carry it) and the sum of all weights (one day). Write canShip(capacity): fill each day greedily and count days. Then run the first-index binary search over that range: if canShip(mid), hi = mid, otherwise lo = mid + 1. Koko Eating Bananas, Split Array Largest Sum and minimum speed problems are this block.

gotchas: Starting lo at 1 instead of the heaviest package, so the check accepts a capacity that can't lift one item.
Getting the direction backwards: when mid works, search left (hi = mid), not right.

complexity.note: The binary search runs log m times over a range of size m (sum minus max), and each check is one O(n) pass.
